title: ITERTL An Iterative Framework for Fine-tuning LLMs for RTL Code Generation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The derivation rewrites min_π Σ_j -log P_π(a_j|...) as min_π Σ_j log(P_teacher(a_j|...)/log P_π(a_j|...)) and then equates this to a KL divergence. This is invalid: -log P_π is not the log-ratio P_teacher/P_π, and the denominator should not be log P_π. The cross-entropy loss is E_{a~π_teacher}[-log π(a)] = KL(P_teacher||π)+constant, not the displayed expression.

The testing protocol chooses the best result across temperatures {0,0.2,0.5,0.8} for each metric on the test set: 'For each test metric (pass@1, pass@5, and pass@10), the best result is chosen.' This is post-hoc test-set tuning and biases the supposedly unbiased pass@k estimator; it also contradicts the earlier statement that they mainly focus on pass@1 under greedy decoding.

The text repeatedly relies on 'As Table 1 shows' for the main benchmark comparisons, but no Table 1 data is present in the paper. The reported SOTA comparisons and 42.9%/62.2% values therefore cannot be verified from the provided document.

The text cites 'Figure 4' for the softmax ablation results, but the paper contains only embedded figures labeled Figure 0 through Figure 3. There is also a text/figure numbering mismatch: the text first references Figure 1, while the first embedded figure is labeled Figure 0.

The text cites many references [1]–[24], but the reference list is essentially missing/corrupted: only one line ('summarize with human feedback. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 33, 3008–3021.') appears. Thus nearly all citations are unverifiable.
